primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Liddle syndrome due to gain-of-function epithelial sodium channel activity
mechanism: Pathogenic variants affecting the ENaC PY motif impair binding of the Nedd4-2 ubiquitin ligase and reduce channel ubiquitination/removal from the apical membrane, increasing ENaC abundance and distal sodium reabsorption. Volume expansion suppresses renin and aldosterone while potassium and hydrogen ion losses cause hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis.
vignette: A 19-year-old man has persistent hypertension despite no obesity or kidney disease. His father developed hypertension as a teenager. Laboratory studies show hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis. Plasma renin activity and aldosterone concentration are both suppressed.
lead: Which of the following molecular changes most directly explains this patient's disorder?
correct: Reduced Nedd4-2-mediated ubiquitination and removal of epithelial sodium channels from the apical membrane
distractors: Constitutive activation of the mineralocorticoid receptor by elevated aldosterone
Loss of the thiazide-sensitive sodium-chloride cotransporter in the distal convoluted tubule
Reduced activity of the sodium-potassium-2 chloride cotransporter in the thick ascending limb
Increased conversion of cortisone to cortisol by renal 11β-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 2
distractor_notes: Aldosterone is suppressed in Liddle syndrome because ENaC-mediated sodium retention causes volume expansion; primary aldosteronism would have elevated aldosterone.
Loss of NCC causes Gitelman syndrome with salt wasting and secondary renin/aldosterone activation rather than low-renin hypertension.
Reduced NKCC2 activity causes a Bartter phenotype with renal salt wasting and elevated renin/aldosterone, not Liddle syndrome.
Renal 11β-HSD2 normally converts cortisol to cortisone; its loss, not increased activity, causes apparent mineralocorticoid excess.
key_expl: In Liddle syndrome, ENaC degradation is impaired. Nedd4-2 normally binds a proline-rich PY motif on ENaC subunits and ubiquitinates the channel for removal. Mutations that disrupt this regulation increase apical ENaC abundance, causing sodium retention, hypertension, potassium wasting, metabolic alkalosis, and suppression of renin and aldosterone.
objective: Relate Liddle syndrome to impaired Nedd4-2/ENaC interaction, reduced ENaC degradation, and low-renin low-aldosterone hypertension.
